  POSITION RELATED THERETO
  Recommendation: The City Council has requested background
  information to assist in determining whether and how to address the
  ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Among the alternative approaches
  for consideration, after public comment, are the following:
  (1) Not take any official position on the ongoing conflict in the Middle
  East; or
  (2) Adopt a policy that the City will not take official positions on any
  non-local, political, or social issues; or
  (3) Adopt a Resolution taking an official position on the ongoing
  conflict in the Middle East; or
  (4) Take any other action determined by the City Council.

  Mayor Gordo announced the rules of decorum for the special meeting;
  he stated that public comment will be limited to one minute per person
  to ensure that everyone has the opportunity to speak.

  City Manager Marquez provided introductory remarks; Assistant City
  Manager Harvey-Williams gave a brief report, and summarized the item
  and staff recommendations as part of a Powerpoint presentation.

Council Minutes  1  03/18/2024
   City Clerk Jomsky reported that the City Clerk's Office received over
  2,000 emails relating to the item. He summarized that there was a large
  number of emails in favor of the City Council adopting a resolution
  calling for a ceasefire, a large number of emails in opposition to the City
  Council acting on this matter, and numerous emails with various
  positions along the spectrum. He stated that the City Clerk's Office
  began posting correspondence in alphabetical order and will continue
  to do so as emails are received, processed for duplication, and
  redacted of personal information. He stated that City staff will make
  best efforts to ensure that all correspondence will be posted online,
  distributed to the City Council, and made part of the public record for
  this item.

  Mayor Gordo thanked the members of the public for their comments
  and re-emphasized the rules of decorum during the City Council's
  discussion on this matter.

  Councilmember Rivas acknowledged that the City should prioritize
  local matters over international affairs, but pointed out that despite the
  City's lack of policy to consider larger issues, the City has addressed
  matters pertaining to foreign affairs (i.e., Proclamation Announcing
  Support for Armenian American Community Members in December

Council Minutes  5  03/18/2024
   2022). She expressed support for the City Council to further discuss
  policy for acting on nonlocal affairs at a later time. She provided a brief
  overview of the resolution she drafted, noting directions to
  congressional representatives and the federal government to utilize
  diplomacy to end the bloodshed. She expressed support for a ceasefire
  resolution and submitted her draft for the City Council's consideration
  and discussion.

  Councilmember Masuda thanked the public for their comments. He
  expressed neutrality on the matter and stated that after reviewing the
  public comments he received by email, he supported the idea that the
  City Council should focus on local needs, and allow congressional
  leaders more informed on international affairs to lead the nation on
  these types of issues. He moved to approve staff recommendation B,
  to adopt a policy that the City will not take official positions on any non-
  local, political, or social issues. Motion failed due to lack of second.

  Councilmember Lyon stated that the City has a history of
  acknowledging issues that are important to the community. He
  expressed support for the City taking a position on a non-local issue
  under three circumstances: if there is demonstrable interest of
  constituents, if the position taken is in the best interest of the City as a
  whole, and if the position taken is fairly representative of the City as a
  whole, where even those who may disagree can recognize the wisdom
  of the decision. He emphasized his role as an elected official is to
  represent his community broadly and the need to utilize language that
  is broadly representative.

  Vice Mayor Madison acknowledged that the City Council is a political
  body and expressed support for taking positions on political issues. He
  advocated for making changes to the resolution proposed by
  Councilmember Rivas to better reflect sentiments on both sides.

  Mayor Gordo advocated for building upon Resolution No. 9831
  (Condemning Hate and Xenophobic Violence Against All Persons),
  which was adopted on March 22, 2021, as a basis for urging the City's
  federal representatives to work towards peace for all. Following
  discussion, Mayor Gordo presented and proposed language for a
  declaration that incorporates sentiment from Resolution No. 9831,
  calling on state and federal leaders to work cooperatively with the
  global community to pursue peace in the Middle East. He noted that
  the proposed language clarifies that the City of Pasadena is supportive
  of peace in every part of the world and urges federal legislators and the
  President to work collaboratively to that end.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Williams,
  seconded by Mayor Gordo, to adopt the proposed declaration.

Council Minutes  6  03/18/2024
   Vice Mayor Madison noted that the language in the proposed
  declaration and does not say anything, and advocated instead to work
  with Councilmember Rivas' proposed resolution instead.

  Councilmember Williams stated that contrary to prior statements that
  the City Council is not a political body, it is rather a body of public
  servants. She emphasized that a resolution is law and expressed
  concerns that the City Council does not have the expertise to propose
  such law pertaining to foreign affairs. She expressed support for
  focusing on policy and Mayor Gordo's proposed declaration.

  At the request of the City Council, Version 1 of the Mayor's proposed
  declaration was distributed to the full City Council and posted on the
  video screen. The Mayor then reviewed the declaration as part of the
  City Council's deliberations.

  Councilmembers Hampton and Jones supported the approach
  proposed by Mayor Gordo, and spoke in agreement with Version 1 of
  Mayor's proposed declaration, which calls for the release of all
  hostages and a ceasefire.

  Councilmember Rivas stated that she cannot support Version 1; she
  referenced the verbiage in the second "Whereas" and stated that if the
  risk of death is imminent, a ceasefire should be called for.

  Councilmember Williams and Mayor Gordo agreed to a friendly
  amendment to approve Version 1, instead of Version 2, of the proposed
  declaration.

  Councilmember Hampton advocated for a short recess to provide the
  City Council with an opportunity to wordsmith Version 1 of the
  declaration.

  Councilmember Rivas made a friendly amendment to the motion to
  implement language in Version 1, Section 2, to state that "the City of
  Pasadena joins other cities calling on leaders at state and federal levels
  to work cooperatively with the global community to release all hostages,
  seek bilateral de-escalation and ceasefire, ensure timely delivery of aid
  to Gaza, and pursue peace in the Middle East to guard and protect the
  lives, health, and security of all innocent civilians."

  Mayor Gordo and Vice Mayor Madison advocated for a friendly
  amendment to remove the verbiage from Section 2 stating that the City
  "joins other cities". Vice Mayor Madison emphasized the need to
  properly assign responsibility, noting that the State leaders are not
  responsible for working on peace in the Middle East. He stated that
  President Biden's Administration is responsible for working on the
  matter and suggested that the declaration give direction for the
  Administration to "continue" their efforts. Mayor Gordo agreed with
  removing "state leaders" from the declaration.

Council Minutes  7  03/18/2024
   Councilmember Williams accepted all friendly amendments and
  suggested changes to the declaration and the current motion.

r  For clarification purposes, City Attorney Bagneris read the declaration
  with the amendments made to Sections 2 and 3:

  "Section 2: The City of Pasadena calls on leaders at the federal level to
  continue to work cooperatively with the global community to release all
  hostages, seek bilateral de-escalation and ceasefire, ensure timely
  delivery of aid to Gaza, and pursue peace in the Middle East to guard
  and protect the lives, health, and security of all innocent civilians."
  "Section 3: The City Council requests a copy of this declaration be sent
  to the offices of Congressmembers Judy Chu and Adam Schiff,
  Senators Alex Padilla and Laphonza Butler, and President Joe Biden."

  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Williams,
  seconded by Mayor Gordo, to approve the proposed declaration as
  amended and detailed above.
